211775.overview: A Tetris variant with 3 levels of difficulty. Each shape that comes out has multiple colors and you can rotate them. Get three in a row to remove the colors.

211805.overview: The worst crisis for Kiwis since the leopard seal incident of 1988! Alien sheep have been kidnapping kiwis all over the country. It's up to you to save your kiwi mates. A fan-sequel to The New Zealand story and itself an almost 1-1 conversion of a freeware PC title from the late 2000s.

211892.overview: A platform shooter developed and released as shareware by Craig Burlock in 1994.

211948.overview: Kaizokuban is a Sokoban clone for all Amiga computers. It's a funny game by AmigaWave & Goblins group for Posadas Party 2018 game compo.

212010.overview: The aim is to sting all the people until they die, while avoiding good bees who will kill us. This simple mechanic gets very quick by level 5, and after level 5 things become frantic and crazy mayhem. A very easy game to understand and play, and fun for those who prefer gameplay over graphics. A great conversion/port of the Odyssey2 game of the same name.

212011.overview: A scrolling multi-directional platform\brawler created by Kyle Hodgetts and published in Oceania by ECP.

212041.overview: You play as the iconic Leatherface from the Texas Chainsaw Massacre movie. Your objective is to kill as many hapless victims as you can before you run out of petrol for your chainsaw. There are petrol canisters that extend playtime in a single round. When you run out of petrol, it is game over and you cycle back to the title screen.

212184.overview:
KickIt is a side-scrolling beat-'em-up for the Amiga. It is a minimalist brawler where there is only one kind of enemy, you have only one kind of attack, there are no weapons or power-ups, and there is no multiplayer mode. The challenge comes from the fact that your attacks always need to be well-timed: taking damage from an enemy is an instant game over, and the enemies move faster and faster as you progress from one area to the next.

The joystick is used to control the Laiban, an enigmatic character who only wears a large, fish-shaped hat. The plot of the game is that the Laiban recently rented a video game from a game rental place across town, and has forgotten to return it in time. In response, the rental place has deployed wave after wave of bloodthirsty zombies, heading straight towards the Laiban. In each area you need to kick every zombie in the face -- you can jump, but not high enough to jump over a zombie -- which causes a bell to ring, signifying that the wave is over, and you can move on to the next area. The ultimate goal is to return the rented game, pacifying the zombie horde.

212185.overview: A public domain game by Paul Ciulla where you use your head to smash through blocks in a certain pattern.

212460.overview: A simple 3 ball billiard game with shot playback and some other nice features.

212461.overview: An R-type style shoot-em up created by Shane Kelly when they were thirteen years old and released in 1993. It has different weapons, smart bomb and a pilot parachute and was created in AMOS.

212468.overview:
As the Federation spread out across the known galaxy, outposts were constructed for scientific research.  These outposts are the life blood for those colonies in the surrounding areas.  While the Federation consists of thousands of worlds, not all races have joined them. Diplomatic relations are always underway to gap the differences and maintain peace.

   The Federation outposts 16, 17 and 18 are close to the boarder of the race called the Krill.  The Krillian are a proud race that prefers isolationism.  Diplomatic relations have become strained recently. Certain fractions within their society have sworn to drive out the Federation from this quadrant by destroying these outposts.  The outposts themselves have limited defense capabilities and can only hold out from a direct assault for a short time.  Your primary assignment will be to defend them against attack. You have also been authorized to destroy all the renegade ships within this quadrant.  Good luck Captain.

212721.overview:
Racing game inspired by a Russian video 'Ustinova - SON' where there is the game 'speed racer'. With graphics and sounds like in an arcade game from 1977, this game challenges you to race against the clock. You get points for distance traveled and cars overtaken. You take damage if you hit the curb or other cars. The game ends when either the time or the damage counter reach zero.

As you drive, the width of the tracks keeps changing. Sometimes you have enough room to overtake cars in front of you. Sometimes the track gets so narrow there is no chance to. When this is the case, you have to slow down to a crawl and bide your time

214011.overview: Meet KIDTALK, the revolutionary talking notebook! Any letters, numbers, words, or sentences you type will be spoken back to you in either a male or female voice. You can let your creative imagination run wild, writing stories, reports, poems, plays and movie scripts. Hear each document spoken back to you for proofreading purposes, for your own critical review or for just plain fun! You control the speech settings including gender, tone, pitch, speed and volume. Each KIDTALK user can develop a Pronunciation Dictionary and Secret Codes that add to the fun! KIDTALK is a perfect tool for the young writer of any age!

214050.overview: Kursk Campaign: Operation Zitadelle is a Strategy / War Simulation game developed and published by Simulations Canada in 1987. The game allows you command in the Kursk Campaign, operation Zitadelle in the summer of 1943. In this command oriented study of the resulting battle, the greatest tank confrontation in history to that point. The axis player must cut into the bulging Soviet line and destroy any trapped Red forces. The Soviet player must blunt this attack with defense in depth and attrite the Axis into defeat. The game includes 2 sets of playing pieces and situation maps for both players. And the computer will act as a player for either side. Scenarios include both early and late Axis offensive start dates. Design by S. St. John, development by S. Newberg, & art by J. Kula.

214100.overview:
Karciarz is a set of four classic card games with all the standard rules implemented:

    358 for three players, divided into 18 rounds with the aim to get the highest score.
    Kierki(Hearts) for three players, divided into 7 rounds with the goal to get the lowest number of penalty points.
    Wist for two players, where the player must gain more tricks (level) in the selected even number of rounds.
    1000 for three players, played with a deck of 24 cards, where the winner is the first collector of a thousand points.

214101.overview: A Kart style racing game with 6 tracks to choose from, created by Axel Illenburg, released to freeware in 1988.

214102.overview:
A new port of  (originally a Philips videopac / Odessey2 game) for the Amiga, released at Amigathon 2018. A top-down maze puzzle game with a concept similar to Pac-Man. The player controls a "Munchkin" whose goal is to eat all of the "munchies" on the screen, all the while being chased by three "Munchers" who are trying to eat him.

By eating a glowing munchie, all of the Munchers will turn purple and can be hunted down for a limited time, successfully doing so results in a score bonus. Once a Muncher has been "munched out" (term used in the manual), it will return to the center of the maze to recharge for a short time before setting out for revenge once again.

As players eat more and more munchies, the remaining munchies begin to move faster and faster around the maze. When there is only one left, it will be moving at the same speed as the player. You'll then have to hunt it down while avoiding the Munchers.

214103.overview: A game based on the ZX Spectrum game, "The Adventures of Sid Spider" originally by David Pegg. This was released as part of the RetroKomp / Load Error 2013 Retro Game competition. Get the keys , grab the treasures and get to the exit to get to the next level. Hammers will allow you to pass through things like barrels.

214104.overview: With graphics inspired by Alien³, this 1997 shareware game from Muzzasoft's Alastair Murray and Ben Wyatt is shooter that had a lot of effort put into it and it shows. A decade earlier this could have been a boxed release. Kill em all is a precursor to Countdown to extinction, which is a precursor to Traitor. If you registered the game for 6 UK Pounds, then you got more levels from the author. The original version was likely from 1993, but we only have the date of the final updates and release.

214105.overview: Kid Pool is a pool\billiards sports game, developed and published by Black Legend, which was released in Europe in 1993.

214106.overview: An AMOS based shareware title from War Production and released in 2000. This is a turn based strategy game for two players from Czechia.  In the full version, the game contains 22 missions, 16 types of units, 4 to 10 music modules, a larger number of sounds and up to 8 missions for two players. The release of the final version of the game was planned for April 2000.

214107.overview: The ruler of the kingdom has passed away. Three dukes, a viking chieftain and the ruler's only heir will now battle for control of the kingdom!!! A strategy game for 0 to 5 players from Absoft Corp and released in 1987.

214108.overview:
King Kong for Amiga is an old remake of the famous Nintendo Game and Watch handheld - "Donkey Kong", which also noted as the first game on two screens. The main idea came from one of the MiniGame compo entries, where it was implemented for Oric. For the Amiga version, new graphics, music and sounds were used. Also the game was rewritten in C and made much easier to port on other platforms. 6 years after the initial release, it was rewritten for the SDL library, thus making it easier to recompile the game source code on much more platforms. For music, the chip music tracker AHX (Abyss Highest Experience) was used. For graphics I used Personal Paint and native Amiga graphics functions, which were later rewritten for the SDL library usage. 

The goal of the game sounds easy - you have to go to the top of the building and catch the crane at the right time. When the crane is catched, a hook holding the King Kong is removed. When all the hooks are removed, the guerilla falls, the player is rewarded bonus points and the happy princess send air kisses to her savior. Several obstacles make the goal harder. The guerilla throws barrels. If a barrel hits the player (or he hits himself in barrel), it takes him a life. There are also patterns on the building site, which can kill our hero, if they hit him. Or the player can fly away from the building, if he does not jump at the right time, or simply go to the wrong way. All these obstacles force the player to come up with a strategy for playing the game and scoring better results, which are kept in the "BEST" score register, shown on the bottom right of the game screen.

The sound effects are minimal, but listening to them are a big helper during the game, where the player adapts to the speed, according to the ticks. The game beside the nice intro screen also have an outro screen, stimulating the player to complete it. The princess starts to smile if the guerilla falls too many times. Bonus lives are rewarded at certain points. There are also some other small surprises, which makes the game a polished product. It can be played with keyboard or Joystick. It is possible to look at the game in window on the Workbench or in full screen mode.

214109.overview: King's Valley is a puzzle platform game in which you need to collect all the treasures by drilling and cutting your way through the pyramids. But beware of the mummies that haunt the pyramids. If you use the limited available cutting and drilling equipment in the wrong order you'll eventually get stuck. You'll then have to play the whole level over again.

214110.overview: A 2D, turn based strategy wargame set in medieval times, created by MBC-Design and released in 1994 as a coverdisk on the 1994-08 on Amigo!. Kings is a simple Laser Squad type of game where you are given troops who must fight the enemy. A good game with great graphics, but too difficult without a manual.

214111.overview: A special Tetris style game, in this one you have to stop the single colored blocks where you want them otherwise they will just disappear and you will lose a life. Line some up and get a Tetris as normal.

214112.overview:
Oh no, Klawz's babe has been cat-napped by the evil Billy Bender. He has to warp through 5 worlds to rescue her...but the evil Billy Bender has set his Robo-Dogs on you, who will try to foil you in your attempt. However, you are not totally helpless, you have your wooden club to bash them on the head with...wow!
Pick ups include B for bonus points, T for time, S for shield. L for speed (Leg it!) and 1 for 1-up extra life.

214113.overview: Klondike, also known as Canfield, is a card game for one player and the best known and most popular version of the patience or solitaire family, something which "defies explanation" as it has one of the lowest rates of success of any such game.

214114.overview: An implementation of the popular "Klondike" form of patience, for the Amiga. It is entirely mousedriven and has online help as well as a monochrome mode. Score is given according to time used; the score counts down for every second spent, and often the score is negative.

214115.overview: The movement of the gamepiece is the same as the knight in chess ( an "L" shape). The goal is to land on all of the squares on the board. It is no easy task....

214117.overview: The pretty pictures are all mixed up. Slide them around like a 15-puzzle until you get the correct orientation to match the miniature. However, there is a limit to the number of moves you have to finish things, so be wise in how to rearrange things.

214118.overview: Köpfchen is a one or two player German puzzle game published by Schatztruhe in 1992.

214119.overview: Konstruktor is a Puzzle game, developed and published by ASF, which was released in Europe in 1993. Includes a level editor. Put the sections of the silver together by the plus signs to join them all together. Once all the pieces are joined at the plusses you can move to the next level.

214120.overview:
Kości zostały rzucone is a computer adaptation of the classic Yahtzee board game. Each turn allows throwing the dices up to three times with replacing unwanted ones. The goal is to fill up a scorecard with all the available sets and the highest score result. Scoring combinations include ones through sixes (school), pair, two pairs, three of a kind, four of kind, full house, small/large straight, even and odd, five of a kind and chance.

The game can be played with up to three players throwing dice in turns.  
 
The game was added as a free bonus in the 1992 release of Skarabeusz.

215124.overview: Kradwaty, a Polish clone of the game Disappearing Balls. Do you remember the "balls" on the PC? Many people have been involved in this simple game. Here's the version for Amiga under the name  Kradwaty or"drews". It had versions in 2014 and an update in 2016.

215231.overview: A solitaire game by David F. Downing released on Amiga Power - Issue 05 - Cover Disk 5 (1991-09)(Future Publishing) in the UK. Players try to get rid of their cards by playing them in a solitaire-like layout of eight piles, built of alternate red and black cards in descending order.

217085.overview: This is a quick build of the SDL shoot-em-up KoboDeluxe for AmigaOS4. Kobo Deluxe is an enhanced version of Akira Higuchi's game XKobo for Un*x systems with X11. Kobo Deluxe adds sound, smoother animation, high resolution support, OpenGL acceleration (optional), an intuitive menu driven user interface, joystick support and other features. Recent versions also add a number of alternative skill levels with slightly modernized gameplay. Kobo Deluxe uses SDL for graphics, sound and input, which makes it possible to build and run the game on pretty much anything.

219294.overview: Kulki translates into walking and is a puzzle game by Krzysztof Koziarek. The game is to arrange the balls in a row. The player arranges five (or more) balls of the same color in a row (horizontally, vertically or diagonally). The player can move the balls to any field that the ball can reach (the ball does not move diagonally).

219378.overview: Arrange your balls so 5 of them line up in order to remove them from the board before the board fills up with balls. Every time you click more balls shown on the side are added to the game board. Choose strategically where to click to move existing balls and to drop the currently loaded set of 3. This version is by Mirq and was released in 2023.

418293.overview: A single player, horizontally scrolling space shooter from Martin Sibernagl.

418534.overview: Using large characters, bright colours and easy to use controls, Kidstype is the ideal starting point for youngsters to both gain confidence in using computers and to create their own stories. Kidstype lets your youngsters add "letter associated" pictures into stories. They can be encouraged to type about the pictures and, if you want it to, Kidstype will speak what has been typed. Kidstype has a spelling game-youngsters can learn to recognise pictures and spell the words associated with the pictures. Based on ideas from teachers, Kidstype is designed to be fun to use and to bring out the creativity in children (and in mums and dads!!)

418554.overview: An action adventure educational clicker created by Frank Andrews of Lawrence Productions.  This game is a sequel to McGee and a precursor to McGee at the Fun Fair.

418737.overview:
Megastyle is proud to release this Amiga version of Kalle Kloakk to you all. This game has been a pain in the neck for me as a coder, there has been tons of moments that I have been thinking of putting this project on ice. But, the bugs and the things that needed to get sorted out with the game has been sorted out. And with good motivation vibes from my team I got it done. 

 So, the Amiga version is based on the same game as the C64 version, the story is the same and you exit to the right as always after all the toilet papers has been picked up. You will see a door when all the paper has been picked up. This is more like  eye candy for your eyes, but, you can still exit anywhere on the right side of the screen. 

The game is built up on a Dual Playfield with 3 bitplanes on each playfield for the extra athmosphere feeling. And the game looks so much better too, better than a black background, won't you agree? 

Anyway; Have fun playing the game!

418814.overview: A single player guess the phrase game, without the "wheel" that would make this a wheel of fortune game. The puzzles for this are in Polish. This is one of 3 different Kolo Szczescia games that came out within about a year in Poland.

418816.overview:
Kelly's rescue
This is part-1 of what has to become a series of 5 adventures, all with the ultimate aim to rescue Kelly.  Kelly is the girl you're in love with and who also works in the national Spy center, just like you do.. You are working as a hail-attendant, the adventure begins in your office, and you are looking forward to the evening when you have a date with Kelly. Special commands in this game are save and restore

Ps: this adventure has first written on the Commodore 64 in 1986 this version is more or less a straight port to the Amiga and it won't contain host of the advanced features of the Amiga but he hope you will like it anyway, part 2 is being written on the Amiga and will have an advanced parser and many other features. Happy adventuring, press any key……..

418819.overview: A single player Wheel of Fortune type game where the puzzles are in Polish.

420633.overview:
The port to the Amiga took 2nd in the Euskal 2023 Open Game competition and was created by Goblins in 2023. Like in the original, our hero must reach Melkhior, a somewhat eccentric wizard who is the only one who can save him. As with most Ultimate titles of the day, reaching him is a long and treacherous challenge, involving both puzzle-solving and action, meaning that each screen requires thorough planning and precise navigation.

The game uses the isometric viewpoint in a manner similar to the later Head Over Heels, using monochrome but detailed graphics and techniques to avoid flickering sprites. The game lasts for 40 days and nights - at night your character turns into a werewolf. Ultimate's individual style of eschewing straightforward instructions in favor of feature lists and riddles is put to good use here, with the story detailed in a rhyming poem of sorts.

420713.overview: An action RPG inspired by Moonstone but still very much in the middle of development.

420884.overview: A top down adventure game demo created by Alex Smyth and Iconic Designs and updated until 1998. It got up to version 0.901 before being abandoned and never finished.

420898.overview: A 1995 unfinished, isomorphic action adventure demo, created by Fred Fish using Blitz Basic but pushed out into the work without being fully formed that others might learn the lessons therein and have a little fun in the process.

420901.overview: Control two huge boxers in this shareware fighting game by Bitstream from 1992.

420947.overview: A single player platform brawler created by Andy Walker with the demo appearing in 1993 with a full release as the cover disk of the UK Amiga magazine The One in June 1994. It is a single player platform game in which the player controls a character in a judo suit. The objective is to kill all the bad guys from each screen in order to progress to the next. The game comprises a series of levels, called floors in the game, with multiple screens or rooms per level. When all the rooms on a floor are cleared the player can progress to the next floor.

421207.overview:
Karate Champ port for Amiga should run on any Amiga with 2MB RAM created by JOTD666 in 2023. Like the original, Karate Champ is an action fighting game for one or two players.

In one player version the player has to master some skills at a karate school to be able to compete in a karate tournament for the national title. At the end of each match is a bonus round where the winner can earn extra points by knocking down flying objects that are tossed his way, breaking roof tiles/ice blocks or knocking down a charging bull on the beach!

In Player vs Player (two player) version, players compete against each other at twelve different locations to see who has the best karate skills! To win a match, the player must win two of three rounds by knocking down his opponent with a wide variety of karate moves. A full point or half a point is awarded for knocking the opponent down and the first player to gain a two point lead wins the round. When the 30 seconds time limit for a round ends, the player who has the most points wins. At the end of each match is a bonus round where the winner can earn extra points by knocking down flying objects that are tossed his way, breaking boards or knocking down charging bulls!

421265.overview:
A few months.I work for the production of Kung Fu master. I am using the Amiga blitzbasic 2.1 language.For the first time I learned the Blitz basic language. I know c language and assembly.I quickly adapted to the blitz basic language.
I started design with level 1.And I've added animation of the game's enemy characters. On the first attempt, I did a short trial of training mode.

422092.overview: Kamikaze Chess (also named Kamikaze Chess or Suicide Chess) is where your objective is to play either a friend or the computer and try to lose all your pieces before your opponent. Released in Amiga Plus cover disks and as one of the 50 Games collection as Suicide Chess.

422162.overview:
A German language, freeware implementation of the Kalaha (aka Mancala) strategy-thinking board game for two players or one human and one computer player, written in AmigaBASIC. The game is played on a board of two rows, each consisting of six round pits. The rows have a large store at either end called the Kalah. A player owns the six pits closest to them and the Kalah on their right side. 
 
The game is started with four (4) seeds in each pit. A player takes all the seeds from one of their pits, and then they are distributed one by one, counterclockwise, in the pits and the player's own Kalah, but not into the opponent's store (Kalah). If the last seed is dropped into an opponent's pit or a non-empty pit of the player, the move ends without anything being captured. If the last seed falls into the player's Kalah, they must move again. If the last seed is put into an empty pit owned by the player, they capture all contents of the opposite pit together with the capturing piece and puts them in their Kalah. If the opposite pit is empty, nothing is captured. A capture ends the move. The game ends when one player no longer has any seeds in any of their holes.

423672.overview:
A freeware conversion of the C64 version of Kaiser to the Amiga in 1988. Kaiser (German for emperor) is a political/business simulation set in 18th century Germany. Players take the role of nobles in the Holy Roman Empire and compete for the crown of the emperor. Gameplay then takes place in turns, each consisting of a number of consecutive screens. In the first screen, players can sell and buy grain and land. Grain is necessary to feed a noble's subjects. Bad weather can result in harvest losses, making it necessary to buy extra grain to prevent starvation. Providing more grain than necessary increases population growth and the state's reputation. Acquiring more land increases population and is necessary for economic growth. Following the trading screen is a statistics screen, displaying births and deaths, immigration and emigration as well as income and expenses.

The third screen allows control of income. Players can set taxes and tariffs and can determine how harshly the justice system works - setting it to a level that is too brutal might increase income in the short term but also lead to increased emigration. Another overview screen follows, displaying a player's lands and properties in detail.

The fifth screen allows for spending the turn's income. It is possible to buy marketplaces and grain mills (both of which increase income) as well as construct part of a palace or a cathedral (both of which have no direct use but are required to move into the highest levels of nobility). Each building option requires owning a certain amount of land. Constructing five marketplaces and three mills results in the creation of a city.

Only if there is more than one player in the game, income can also be spent on military expenses. Soldiers can be recruited from the own population or hired as mercenaries. Recruitment is limited by population size, while mercenaries cost more, but are more skilled from the start. Infantry, cavalry and artillery units are available. Military exercises can be conducted to increase the troops' experience. Finally, troops can be sent to war by selecting another player to attack. Only geographical neighbors can be attacked directly - if other states are in the way, their regents have to be asked for right of passage. All other players besides the two fighting parties are asked if they want to support either of the two. If a party gains the support of another noble, they are allowed to control the supporting player's troops in the battle. The actual battle is fought automatically, but both parties can place their troops on a map of the defending player's lands beforehand. The victor of a battle gains land from the loser.

At the end of a turn, interest on the money reserves (or the debt) is calculated and players move ahead in the ranks of the nobility if certain winning conditions are met. Higher ranks increase the debt limit and allow players to be more demanding in setting taxes.
